title: What are Primitive Types in Patterns (JEP 507) for instanceof/switch?
shortTitle: What are Primitive Types in Patterns?
keyPoints: JEP 507 extends pattern matching to primitive types: instanceof and switch now work with int, long, float, and double
Safe narrowing: if (longVal instanceof int i) succeeds only if the value fits in an int without loss
Switch can match on long, float, and double values with guards: case int i when i > 0 -> ...
Eliminates manual range checks and explicit casts when deciding how to store numeric values
Completes the pattern matching story: reference patterns (Java 16-21) plus primitive patterns (Java 24)
Exhaustiveness checking works with primitive patterns over sealed types

s1_definition.oneliner: Primitive types in patterns (JEP 507) extends instanceof and switch to match primitive types like int, long, and double with safe narrowing conversions.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Primitive patterns** – `instanceof` and `switch` now match against primitive types, not just reference types.
- **Safe narrowing** – `if (longVal instanceof int i)` succeeds only if the long value fits in an int without data loss.
- **Switch on long/double** – `switch` can now match on `long`, `float`, and `double` values, not just `int`, `String`, and `enum`.
- **Guards** – `case int i when i > 0 -> ...` combines type matching with conditions on primitive values.
- **Unification** – completes the pattern matching model so it covers both reference and primitive types uniformly.
s1_definition.analogy: Before, the bank's routing system could only sort by customer name (reference types). After JEP 507, it can also sort by account number (int), balance (double), and transaction amount (long) directly in the routing rules.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Primitive Types in Patterns (JEP 507, Java 24 preview) extends pattern matching to primitive types. You can now write `if (longVal instanceof int i)` for safe narrowing that only matches when the value fits without data loss. Switch expressions can match on long, float, and double with guards, not just int, String, and enum.

This eliminates manual range checks and explicit casts. Before JEP 507, checking if a long fits in an int required `amount >= Integer.MIN_VALUE && amount <= Integer.MAX_VALUE` followed by a cast. Now a single pattern match does both the check and the binding.

The feature completes the pattern matching story: reference patterns (Java 16-21) handle objects and records, and primitive patterns (Java 24) handle numeric types. Together, they give Java a unified pattern matching model across all types.

Remember one sentence: primitive patterns extend instanceof and switch to match int, long, and double with safe narrowing, completing the pattern matching unification.
